storyline.latest_title: Same Model, Different Harness: CUGA, Hermes, and Deep Agents — When to Pick CUGA?

prior_narrative.tldr: Most of this thread shares a "Same X, Different Y" title pattern, not one event. Three arXiv papers (Oct 22-26) cover chemistry identifier binding, credit assignment for agentic RL and news framing; a Nov 1 post then reported a 17-point gap between agents using one model.
prior_narrative.whats_new: On Nov 3, an IBM Research Hugging Face post compared CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents on the same model, asking when to pick CUGA.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Two harness-versus-model posts in three days make the same point: the agent harness can move results as much as the model, so evaluate the full stack.

status.detail: Title-match papers are coincidental; the Nov 1 and Nov 3 posts form the real thread on harness effects.

beats.headline: Two arXiv papers on reliability and agentic RL
beats.summary: Identifier binding failures in chemistry LLMs, and twin-world credit assignment for agentic RL.

beats.headline: Same model, different agent: 17 points apart on 21 MCP servers

beats.headline: IBM Research compares CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents on one model
beats.summary: A vendor harness comparison on Hugging Face.

open_questions: Does the MCP post publish its harness differences, prompts and scoring method so the 17-point gap can be reproduced?
Does the IBM CUGA post report numbers on a shared benchmark, and can they be rerun?
Do any of the arXiv papers release code or evals that apply to tool-using agents?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Hold the model fixed and vary the harness in your own eval on your MCP servers; treat the 17-point figure and IBM's CUGA comparison as vendor or blog results until reproduced.

day_captions.615493c68bfd12ef: Studies whether co-referring molecule identifiers (names, IUPAC, SMILES) are treated as interchangeable by LLMs.
day_captions.352167f7ac41065b: Proposes twin-world counterfactual branching to assign credit to individual decisions in agentic RL episodes.
day_captions.40a1feed41fe68a1: Presents a research prototype comparing what outlets emphasize and omit when covering the same event.
day_captions.b78023b26122d472: Blog post whose title reports a 17-point spread between agents using the same model on 21 MCP servers.
day_captions.b05fd13d79e76b34: IBM Research frames CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents as harnesses around one model and asks when to choose CUGA.
